request.system:
You classify one recorded call at Aegis Cloud Security, a B2B SaaS company, against a fixed theme taxonomy (version v1).

You receive the full transcript as numbered turns in the form "[index] Speaker (side): sentence". side is "customer" (works at an outside company) or "aegis_staff" (works at Aegis). You are given nothing else about the call: no title, no call type, no summary. Judge only from the words in the transcript.

THEMES (what kind of conversation it is; pick by what the call is mostly about):
1. Commercial Renewals and Retention: Renewals, contracts, pricing and SLA negotiation, churn risk, expansion deals. Boundary: If a call is mainly about product adoption with renewal as an aside, use Product Adoption, Feedback and Expansion.
2. Product Adoption, Feedback and Expansion: Previews, launches, early access, roadmap input, feature requests, adoption and compliance-readiness reviews of the product, and internal launch-readiness reviews. Boundary: The module belongs in the product area field, not in the theme. Renewal talk that is only an aside stays here.
3. Incident and Outage Response: War rooms, root cause, remediation plans, customer impact assessment, incident communication, postmortems, reliability reviews. Boundary: A single customer's technical fault that is not a platform incident belongs in Technical Integration and Performance Issues.
4. Technical Integration and Performance Issues: Support-style troubleshooting: SSO, SAML, SCIM, LDAP, MFA failures, connectors and SIEM integration, backup windows and throughput, report defects, API errors, internal scalability concerns. Boundary: Module-specific problems go here with the module in the product area field. A platform-wide outage is Incident and Outage Response.
5. Onboarding and Implementation Scoping: Kickoffs, deployment planning, architecture scoping, setup workshops. Boundary: Troubleshooting of an already deployed integration is Technical Integration and Performance Issues.
6. Billing and Usage Disputes: Invoices, overages, seat counts, billing adjustments. Boundary: Small theme (about 4 calls in the pilot); kept because it is distinct and actionable.
7. Competitive Strategy and Win/Loss: Competitive intelligence, battlecards, win/loss analysis, and customer-facing calls where the customer is evaluating alternatives. Boundary: Definition widened from the pilot's internal-only version to include customer calls about evaluating alternatives.
8. Internal Planning and Delivery Cadence: Standups, sprint planning, retros, all-hands, design and roadmap syncs with no customer or incident focus. Boundary: If a meeting is mainly an incident, use Incident and Outage Response.

Other / new theme: use only if no theme above fits. Then describe the call in one sentence in other_description. Other / new theme only if no theme fits. More than 10% of calls in Other triggers a taxonomy revision (new version, full re-run).

PRODUCT AREA (which module the call is about; exactly one):
- Detect: Threat detection, event ingestion, alerting.
- Comply: Compliance reporting and evidence mapping (including Comply v2).
- Protect: Backup, snapshots, disaster recovery (includes backup).
- Identity: Directory sync, SSO, SAML, SCIM, MFA, IAM governance.
- Platform/General: No single product dominates, or the call is cross-product.

INCIDENT: Set incident to '2026-03-detect-outage' (otherwise null) when the call's main purpose, or a major part of it, is the March 2026 Detect event-processing pipeline outage: cause, impact, remediation, customer communication or aftermath. A separate field so the outage story is visible across support, external and internal calls.

Return one record with:
- primary_theme: exactly one theme name copied from the list above, or "Other / new theme".
- tags: zero, one or two further theme names from the list that also clearly come up. Never repeat the primary theme. Empty when primary_theme is "Other / new theme".
- product_area: exactly one product area name copied from the list.
- incident: "2026-03-detect-outage" or null.
- other_description: one sentence if primary_theme is "Other / new theme", otherwise an empty string.
- evidence_quote: a short passage of at most 30 words that best supports primary_theme, copied EXACTLY, character for character, from the sentence part of ONE turn. Copy only the words after "Speaker (side): ". Never include the index, the speaker name, the side or the colon prefix. Do not paraphrase, do not shorten with "...", do not join text from different turns.
- confidence: "high" if clearly about the primary theme, "medium" if two themes compete, "low" if it fits poorly.
- taxonomy_version: "v1".

Return only JSON matching the schema.

[13] Raymond Burke (customer): Yes, that is something I definitely want to get into, but maybe let me give you a bit more context first on what our environment actually looks like.
[14] Aisha Johnson (aegis_staff): Please, yes, go ahead.
[15] Raymond Burke (customer): So we've got roughly four hundred and fifty virtual machines across our on-prem data centers — two locations, one in Chicago, one in Denver — and then we've got a growing CloudPrime footprint, probably around eighty EC2 instances right now with RDS databases, and we're also using some S3 for unstructured data, imaging files mostly, which in healthcare as you can imagine is enormous.

[18] Aisha Johnson (aegis_staff): Okay, that's really helpful context — so when you think about recovery objectives, what does your current RTO and RPO look like for your most critical systems, like your EHR for example?
[19] Raymond Burke (customer): So this is actually where it gets a little embarrassing — our documented RTO for the EHR is four hours, RPO is one hour, but I will tell you candidly that we have never actually tested a full restore at that scale and I have very low confidence that we'd hit those numbers with our current tooling.
[20] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): I really appreciate you being upfront about that Raymond because that is honestly more common than people admit, and the good news is that's exactly the kind of thing we can help you get to a place of actual confidence on.
[21] Raymond Burke (customer): Yeah and that's, that's really what I want — I want to be able to walk into my CISO's office and say look, we have tested this, we know it works, here's the evidence, rather than just hoping we never have to find out.
[22] Aisha Johnson (aegis_staff): So Aegis Protect has an automated recovery testing feature — essentially it can spin up isolated sandbox environments and run restore validation on a scheduled basis, and you get reports that show you actual recovery time metrics against your defined objectives, which is something your CISO is going to love.
[23] Raymond Burke (customer): Wait, it actually runs the test automatically? Like I don't have to schedule a maintenance window and have my team babysit it?
[24] Aisha Johnson (aegis_staff): That's right — you configure the schedule, define the recovery objectives, and the platform handles the orchestration, and then you get a report in your dashboard with pass/fail status and the actual measured RTOs.
[25] Raymond Burke (customer): Okay that is genuinely exciting because our current process for even attempting a restore test is like a whole weekend project that nobody wants to volunteer for.
[26] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Ha, yeah I have heard that from so many customers, the restore test that never happens because it's too painful to run.
[27] Raymond Burke (customer): Exactly, so let's talk about the hybrid piece because that's maybe my biggest concern — can Aegis Protect actually manage backups across the on-prem VMware environment and CloudPrime from a single pane of glass?
[28] Aisha Johnson (aegis_staff): Yes, that's a core capability — there's a lightweight agent that deploys to your on-prem hosts and it feeds into the same Aegis Protect console where you're managing your CloudPrime workloads, so you get unified visibility, unified policy management, and unified reporting all in one place.
[29] Raymond Burke (customer): And for the VMware side specifically, does it do image-level backups or are we talking agent-based on each VM?

[38] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): And all of that archived data is encrypted with keys that you control — we support bring your own key if your compliance posture requires that level of control.
[39] Raymond Burke (customer): BYOK support is something our security team is going to ask about for sure, so good to have that in my back pocket.
[40] Aisha Johnson (aegis_staff): Okay so let me just kind of summarize where I think we are and then we can talk about next steps — Raymond, it sounds like your primary priorities are getting unified backup coverage across hybrid, getting to tested and documented RTOs you can actually stand behind, handling tiered retention for compliance, and making sure the HIPAA encryption requirements are covered, does that feel right?
[41] Raymond Burke (customer): Yeah that's a really good summary, and I'd add one more which is just overall visibility — I want to know at any given moment what is backed up, when was the last successful backup, what's the status, without having to dig through multiple tools.
[42] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Love that addition, and the Aegis Protect dashboard is very much built around that operational visibility use case, we can actually do a deeper demo of the dashboard UI in our next session if that would be helpful.
[43] Raymond Burke (customer): Yes, absolutely, and can we also get into the implementation timeline? I want to understand what the rollout looks like and what we need from our side to make it go smoothly.
[44] Aisha Johnson (aegis_staff): Definitely — what I'll do is put together a proposed implementation plan based on everything we've discussed today, I'm thinking a phased approach where we start with your CloudPrime workloads since those are newer and probably faster to onboard, and then tackle the on-prem VMware environment in phase two, does that logic make sense?
[45] Raymond Burke (customer): Yeah that makes a lot of sense, get some wins under our belt on the cloud side and then work through the more complex on-prem piece.
[46] Aisha Johnson (aegis_staff): Exactly, and I'll also include some pre-work items for your team — things like network access requirements, vSphere API credentials, IAM roles on the CloudPrime side — so you're not surprised by any dependencies when we kick off.
[47] Raymond Burke (customer): That is really appreciated, the checklist approach is helpful because I can distribute that to my team and we can start getting stuff lined up in parallel.
[48] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Raymond this has been such a great conversation, I feel like we've got a really solid foundation to build from — is there anything else you want to make sure we covered before we wrap up?
[49] Raymond Burke (customer): I think we got what I needed for today, honestly more than I expected — I'm going to loop in my infrastructure lead for the next session so she can dig into the technical details on the VMware integration side.
[50] Aisha Johnson (aegis_staff): Perfect, yes please bring her in, the more technical context we have the better the implementation plan will be.
[51] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Alright, I'll get a follow-up invite on the calendar for next week, I'll send over the implementation plan draft and the dashboard demo agenda before then so you and your team can review ahead of time.
[52] Raymond Burke (customer): Sounds great, I'm really looking forward to it — thanks Lisa, thanks Aisha, this was a really productive session.
[53] Aisha Johnson (aegis_staff): Thank you Raymond, we're really excited to be working with Vanta Health on this, talk soon!
[54] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Take care Raymond, we'll be in touch!
